title: Wren and the Cipher
premise: Ada Eastwick, a true-crime podcaster who has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidents, reopens the case of Wren Calloway, a missing archivist whose diary inexplicably contains entries written after her disappearance. Following the diary's coded references, Ada and her found family of collaborators are pulled into a conspiracy surrounding a decades-old trial everyone believed was closed, where each cipher they decode costs someone their safety. As duty to the truth collides with love for the people now marked by it, Ada must choose between exposing the killer and protecting the family she never had. In the end, Ada closes the case on air at the trial's eve, trading her anonymity and nearly her life for justice, while Wren—alive in hiding—finally comes home.
about_author: Sebastian Delacroix is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing trials before turning to fiction. They write mysteries from a coastal town that has never once appeared on a map they were allowed to keep.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. While preparing an episode on Wren Calloway's twenty-year-old disappearance, Ada discovers the archived diary continues three weeks past the date police closed the case. The beat is cold dread: the coldest case just got warmer.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback-tinged. We learn how Ada solved three 'accidental' deaths through her podcast, earning a small loyal team: researcher Juno, retired detective Marsh, and sound engineer Theo. Beat: found family established, and its fragility hinted.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The post-disappearance diary entries contain margin symbols matching an archivist's shorthand. Juno decodes the first phrase: 'They know I copied it.' Beat: the case shifts from mystery to warning.

chapters.title: The Closed Trial
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Marsh recalls the Hollis trial—the corruption case Wren worked as court archivist—dismissed for evidence tampering. He recognizes the diary's codes reference sealed exhibits. Beat: old guilt surfaces; he testified in that courtroom.

chapters.title: Someone Is Listening
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After the episode teaser drops, Theo isolates background noise from a voicemail tip and identifies surveillance equipment—a professional recording Ada's calls. Beat: paranoia enters the household; the family tightens ranks.

chapters.title: Wren's Apartment, Sealed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Breaking into the long-sealed apartment, Ada finds a second diary hidden in a floor cavity, addressed 'For whoever keeps asking.' It names a dead man as still alive. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Investigating 'dead' witness Elias Vann, Juno finds his death certificate forged by the same clerk who mishandled the Hollis exhibits. Beat: the conspiracy has institutional roots, not just one villain.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Marsh confesses he buried a discrepancy in the Hollis trial to protect his dying partner's pension. Ada's fury fractures the family. Beat: love against duty—loyalty tested by honesty.

chapters.title: Entry Forty-One
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Diary entry forty-one describes a safe deposit box and warns 'the third accident is a rehearsal.' Ada realizes the earlier deaths she solved were practice runs by the same hand. Beat: personal stakes become mortal ones.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Harbor Road
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo spots their tail during a records run and executes a counter-surveillance route learned from a misspent youth. Beat: competence and camaraderie; the family begins to heal.

chapters.title: The Deposit Box
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Inside the box: microfilm of the original Hollis exhibits and a photograph of Wren taken two years ago—alive, older, watching. Beat: hope detonates; Wren may be hiding by choice.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Number Four
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A near-fatal 'accident' targets Juno, confirming the pattern and the killer's identity profile: someone with courtroom access. Beat: terror and resolve; no one is disposable anymore.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Confession
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Marsh confronts the retired clerk, who admits selling exhibit access but swears he never touched the diary—and that Wren came to him frightened, not fleeing. Beat: the hunted becomes the hunter's quarry.

chapters.title: Cipher Broken
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno cracks the full cipher: the diary entries past the disappearance were written by Wren herself, in anticipation, as insurance. Beat: awe—Wren planned her own vanishing to survive.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A prosecutor quietly reopening Hollis subpoenas Ada's research, forcing a deadline: produce real evidence or the case dies and the killer walks free. Beat: duty returns with teeth.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A charming fixer offers Ada money and safety to hand over the microfilm, revealing the killer's reach—and accidentally confirming which judge is compromised. Beat: temptation met with defiance.

chapters.title: Where Wren Went
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the diary's final geographic riddle, Ada finds Wren living under a new name. Wren explains: testifying meant death; silence meant the guilty stayed free. Beat: two survivors recognize each other.

chapters.title: Love Against Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (first time). Wren weighs coming forward against losing everything again, watching Ada risk her family daily. Beat: Wren chooses courage because someone finally kept asking.

chapters.title: The Trap They Built Together
chapters.summary: Full cast POV rotation. The team stages a leak to draw the killer into destroying the last original exhibit, recording everything. Beat: the hunted set the snare; tension at breaking point.

chapters.title: Night at the Records Hall
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The killer—Judge Aldous Renner's clerk, covering for Renner himself—springs the trap backward; Marsh takes a bullet shielding Wren. Ada captures the confession on Theo's hidden mics. Beat: climax; sacrifice and exposure intertwined.

chapters.title: Closing Arguments
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. At the reopened Hollis hearing, the recordings land, Renner falls, and Marsh survives recovery surrounded by the family he once lied to. Beat: catharsis; duty and love reconciled.

chapters.title: Episode One Hundred
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the hundredth episode, Ada tells the whole story, then goes off-air to a kitchen full of people who stayed—including Wren, writing again, this time in plain language. Beat: resolution; survival's price paid, and worth it.
